# Generated by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic)
Plan — "Yol B": non-invasive application-symbol probes to VERIFY join internals
=============================================================================
Written 2026-08-17. Status: PLANNED, not started. Companion to
notes/join_semantics_from_traces.txt (what ROS-level tracing can/cannot tell)
and postprocess/join_analysis.py (what we measure today).

Why
---
FISH detects a join structurally (≥2 sibling input callbacks publish the same
output) and measures its trigger semantics per instance (completer split,
bimodal cost, AND test). Two things stay out of reach of the ROS layer:
  1. Per-instance PROOF that every completed set contained one message from
     each member (we have ~90 % + all timeouts incomplete — evidence, not
     proof; no frame/collector id in the trace, stamps are not traced).
  2. DATA dependency without TRIGGER dependency ("latest-value fusion":
     run on every A, read buffered B/C) — invisible at ROS level.
Both live in application memory. The application's own functions, however,
are visible symbols in its shared library — and can be probed at runtime
without changing or rebuilding anything.

What is available (checked 2026-08-17 in autoware-dev-trt-a1000-fishwait5)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Autoware concat libs are NOT stripped; the join internals are exported
(weak) symbols, e.g. in /opt/autoware/lib/libconcatenate_data.so:
  autoware::pointcloud_preprocessor::CloudCollector<PointCloud2Traits>::process_pointcloud(...)   @0xaf660
  autoware::pointcloud_preprocessor::CloudCollector<PointCloud2Traits>::concatenate_callback()     @0xaefb0
(CUDA variants in libcuda_pointcloud_preprocessor*.so with CudaPointCloud2Traits.)
process_pointcloud(this, topic_name, cloud) is called once per deposit;
concatenate_callback(this) once per completion (input-completed OR timeout).
`this` = the CloudCollector = the FRAME identity we lack.

Tooling options
---------------
A) perf uprobes (preferred for arguments):
     perf probe -x /opt/autoware/lib/libconcatenate_data.so \
       'CloudCollector<...>::process_pointcloud this topic_name'      # entry, args
     perf probe -x ... 'CloudCollector<...>::concatenate_callback this'
     perf probe -x ... 'CloudCollector<...>::concatenate_callback%return'
     perf record -e probe_lib...:* -a --clockid CLOCK_MONOTONIC ...   # same clock as LTTng-UST
   Gives (ts, pid, tid, this, topic_name) per deposit and (ts, this) per
   completion. perf is NOT installed in the Autoware images (apt:
   linux-tools-generic or build from kernel src for the host kernel 6.8);
   uprobes need CAP_SYS_ADMIN / --privileged (we already run privileged).
   Debuginfo not required for arguments if we probe by symbol + register
   convention (x86-64: this=%di, topic_name=%si) — perf probe accepts
   '%di:u64 %si:string' style specs without DWARF.
B) LTTng kernel userspace-probe (same session as our UST trace, one clock):
     lttng enable-event -k --userspace-probe=elf:/opt/autoware/lib/libconcatenate_data.so:<mangled sym> ev_name
   Entry hits only (no args) — enough for "which thread hit concatenate_callback
   when" (completer identity from thread + timestamp) but NOT for `this`.
   Needs lttng-modules on the HOST kernel (kernel domain); container has the
   CLI, host needs the modules. Check: lsmod | grep lttng.
C) bpftrace/eBPF uprobes: `bpftrace -e 'uprobe:/opt/autoware/lib/libconcatenate_data.so:<sym> { printf("%d %s %p\n", tid, ...) }'`
   Also captures args by register; needs bpftrace in image or on host
   (host-side attach works across containers by binary path in the container
   rootfs: /proc/<pid>/root/opt/autoware/lib/...). Probably the quickest.

Plan (one afternoon)
--------------------
1. Symbol inventory: nm -DC of the concat libs → exact mangled names for the
   two methods (both Traits). Confirm ABI: `this` in %rdi, topic_name (const
   std::string&) in %rsi → dereference _M_p for the char*.
2. Attach from the HOST with bpftrace (option C) to the r10b-style run:
     - uprobe process_pointcloud: emit (ts_mono, pid, tid, this, topic)
     - uprobe concatenate_callback: emit (ts_mono, pid, tid, this)
     - uretprobe concatenate_callback: (ts_mono, tid) → merge duration
   Write to session_dir/fishlog/uprobes.jsonl. Clock: bpftrace `nsecs` is
   CLOCK_MONOTONIC (boot-based on some kernels — verify against an LTTng
   event: match a known callback_start on the same tid).
3. Join proof: for each concatenate_callback(this=C): the set of
   process_pointcloud(this=C, topic) since C's previous completion must be
   {right,left,top} for input-completed ones and a strict subset for timer
   ones. Report per-frame membership EXACTLY; compare with join_analysis'
   statistical AND test (expect: the 22 "undetermined" resolve to complete).
4. Data-dependency probe (Case 1a-vs-latest-value): for a fusion node,
   probe the buffer READ accessor (e.g. get_latest_*()) inside the trigger
   callback — if the read hits inputs other than the trigger's, it is a
   latest-value data dependency; annotate the F with data_deps=[...].
5. Fold results into FISH as an OPTIONAL "join verification" instrument
   (fish_settings.ini [probes] symbols = ...; run script attaches
   bpftrace; ingest_pg loads uprobes.jsonl into a `uprobe_events` table;
   join_analysis --with-uprobes prints exact per-frame membership).
6. Overhead: measure with/without probes on the same run (probe cost ~1 µs
   per hit; concat sees ~900 deposits + 270 completions in 60 s → negligible)
   and record it in the probe-effect harness table.

Constraints / positioning
-------------------------
- This is application-specific by construction (symbol names per node type).
  It is NOT the general FISH pipeline; it is the verification instrument
  that FISH points to once it has detected a join structurally. Keep it
  optional and documented as such.
- The Aug-2026 handoff closed "perf/uftrace as general callback-internal
  tracing". Uprobes on 2-3 named symbols for join verification is a
  different, narrower use — say so explicitly in the paper.
- Non-invasive: no source change, no rebuild, image immutable, probes
  attach to a running process (fresh container as always).
